findings.F1: Inside the falling calm profile, the tested idea's grading holds clearly on the explore half: the slope of the coin's 7-day excess return on its 14-day return scaled by the 30-day mean high-low range has a t of 3.58 (61 non-overlapping cases, Spearman 0.33). Cases with a positive scaled rise gain +5.1 % over the coin's drift (t 2.34, 21 cases).
findings.F2: The same scaled 14-day move grades weaker at other horizons: t 2.44 over 3 days (155 cases, Spearman 0.16, mean of the rising cases +1.05 %, t 1.38) and t 1.15 over 14 days (25 cases). The 7-day horizon the idea uses is where it is clearest.
findings.F3: The other angles give nothing that stands out beyond chance after about 25 groupings:
findings.F4: The only large quintile gap is on the short side, outside this research's long-only box: the second-lowest 14-day-return quintile loses -7.6 % over the next 7 days (t -2.07, 15 cases), and the lowest loses -3.1 %.

ideas.name: calm downtrend rise continues
ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, a coin that has risen over the last 14 days keeps rising over the next 7 days, and rises further the larger its 14-day rise is in units of its 30-day average daily high-low range.
ideas.consequence: An unusual two-week rise inside a calm downtrend is a reason to buy for about a week, and to buy more the larger the rise is against the coin's usual range.
